newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Clinton hails EU joining N.Korean nuclear plan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails EU joining N.Korean nuclear plan.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Wednesday welcomed a European Union decision to join efforts to break up North Korea's nuclear capacity.

"This will help us to make good on our commitment to freeze and to eventually dismantle North Korea's dangerous nuclear programme," the American leader told a news conference after EU-U.S. talks with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and European Commission President Jacques Santer.

A spokesman for the Commission, the 15-nation bloc's executive body, said last week that EU membership of the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) was of "enormous political and financial significance".
"It shows for the first time that we do not only have a commercial interest in East-Asia but a strategic interest to promote peace and security there," he said.

KEDO was set up two years ago by the United States, Japan and South Korea to help North Korea develop its nuclear energy industry while at the same time ensuring its reactors were not diverted to non-energy activities.

Stephen Bosworth, KEDO's executive director, has said the EU's proposed contribution of 75 million ecus ($86 million) over five years to the $5 billion international scheme will make European companies eligible to bid for contracts "worth substantially more".
